paper.title: CRYSTALFORMER: INFINITELY CONNECTED ATTENTION FOR PERIODIC STRUCTURE ENCODING
paper.research_summary: Predicting physical properties of materials from their crystal structures is a fundamental problem in materials science. In peripheral areas such as the prediction of molecular properties, fully connected attention networks have been shown to be successful. However, unlike these finite atom arrangements, crystal structures are infinitely repeating, periodic arrangements of atoms, whose fully connected attention results in infinitely connected attention.

tasks.task_name_raw: Predicting physical properties of materials from their crystal structures
tasks.objective: Predicting physical properties of materials from their crystal structures without actually synthesizing materials is important for accelerating the discovery of new materials with desired properties
input_requirements: crystal structures represented as unit cell points and lattice vectors
output_goal: predicted physical property values for crystal structures

evidence.text: Predicting physical properties of materials from their crystal structures is a fundamental problem in materials science.
We consider a problem of estimating physical properties of a given crystal structure.
We perform regression tasks of several important material properties, comparing with several neural-network-based state-of-the-art methods

stages.stage_name_raw: Using Materials Project and JARVIS-DFT datasets
stages.stage_goal: Acquire crystal structure data with DFT-calculated properties for training and evaluation

evidence.text: Materials Project (MEGNet) is a collection of 69,239 materials from the Materials Project database retrieved by Chen et al. (2019). Following Yan et al. (2022), we perform regression tasks of formation energy, bandgap, bulk modulus, and shear modulus.

JARVIS-DFT (3D 2021) is a collection of 55,723 materials by Choudhary et al. (2020). Following Yan et al. (2022), we perform regression tasks of formation energy, total energy, bandgap, and energy above hull (E hull).

stages.stage_name_raw: Representing crystal structures with unit cell points and lattice vectors
stages.stage_goal: Prepare crystal structure representations that capture periodicity and spatial relationships
stage_output: unit cell points P = {p1, p2, ..., pN}

evidence.text: Assume a periodic structure system on a lattice in 3D space, which consists of finite sets of points and their attributes, P = {p1, p2, ..., pN} and X 0 = {x0_1, x0_2, ..., x0_N}, in a unit cell as well as lattice vectors, l1, l2, l3 ∈R3, defining the unit cell translations.

stages.stage_name_raw: Training Crystalformer model with stochastic gradient descent
stages.stage_goal: Train the Crystalformer architecture to learn mappings from crystal structures to physical properties

evidence.text: For each regression task in the Materials Project dataset, we train our model by optimizing the mean absolute error loss function via stochastic gradient descent (SGD) with a batch size of 128 materials for 500 epochs.

stages.stage_name_raw: Evaluating model performance on property regression tasks
stages.stage_goal: Assess the trained model's accuracy on predicting various crystal properties
stage_output: mean absolute errors (MAEs) for property predictions
